system_prompt:
You are solving a controlled benchmark task.
You may only use the available tools.
Do not assume internet access.
Do not access files outside the workspace.
Do not invent unavailable data.
Produce the required output files.
When finished, call submit.

Protocol rules:
- Reply with exactly one <tool_call> block per turn.
- Do not write prose, markdown, or code outside the <tool_call> block.
- The JSON inside <tool_call> must be one object with exactly two top-level fields: "tool" and "args".
- The "tool" field must be a string: "read", "write", "edit", "bash", or "submit".
- The "args" field must be an object.
- Tool results can be long. Do not copy tool-result content into your reply; choose the next tool call.
- For multi-line Python, use write to create a script, then bash to run it; avoid giant inline bash commands.

Available tools and argument schemas:
- read: {"path": "relative/path.txt"} or {"path": "relative/path.txt", "max_chars": 12000}
- write: {"path": "relative/path.txt", "content": "complete file content"}
- edit: {"path": "relative/path.txt", "old": "text to replace", "new": "replacement text", "replace_all": true}
- bash: {"command": "python src/solution.py"}
- submit: {"message": "done"}

Valid examples:
<tool_call>
{"tool": "read", "args": {"path": "inputs/example.csv"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_call>
{"tool": "write", "args": {"path": "outputs/example.txt", "content": "complete file content"}}
</tool_call>

Invalid examples:
- {"tool": {"args": {"path": "inputs/example.csv"}}}
- {"read": {"path": "inputs/example.csv"}}
- prose before or after the <tool_call> block
- copying a CSV or script into the response without using the write tool

Use this exact shape for every response:
<tool_call>
{"tool": "...", "args": {...}}
</tool_call>
task_prompt:
Task ID: T15
Title: Produce reproducible report and figures
Family: validation_reporting

Generate a reproducible Markdown report and two distinct non-empty figures without unsupported claims.

Available input files:
- all previous outputs

Required output files:
- reports/pipeline_report.md
- figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png
- figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png

Output requirements:
- reports/pipeline_report.md:
  - Markdown sections: # Overview, # Input data, # Methods, # Generated outputs, # Main results, # Limitations, # Reproducibility
  - Each section must contain at least one sentence (at least 80 characters of text).
  - Reference the pipeline artifacts by their paths under outputs/.
  - Do not claim live API access.
- figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png:
  - Non-empty PNG image of at least 400x300 pixels.
- figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png:
  - Non-empty PNG image of at least 400x300 pixels, distinct from the other figure.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

root = Path(".")
checks = []

outputs = {
    "t01_selected_indicators": root / "outputs" / "t01_selected_indicators.csv",
    "t05_clean_stops": root / "outputs" / "t05_clean_stops.csv",
    "t08_pois_clean": root / "outputs" / "t08_pois_clean.csv",
    "t10_accessibility_scores": root / "outputs" / "t10_accessibility_scores.csv",
    "t13_city_clusters": root / "outputs" / "t13_city_clusters.csv",
}

readable = {}
for name, path in outputs.items():
    if not path.exists():
        readable[name] = False
        checks.append({"check_name": f"{name}_present", "passed": False, "message": f"{path} is missing."})
    elif path.stat().st_size == 0:
        readable[name] = False
        checks.append({"check_name": f"{name}_present", "passed": False, "message": f"{path} is empty."})
    else:
        readable[name] = True
        checks.append({"check_name": f"{name}_present", "passed": True, "message": f"{path} is present and non-empty."})

if readable["t05_clean_stops"]:
    stops = pd.read_csv(outputs["t05_clean_stops"])
    checks.append({"check_name": "t05_clean_stops_columns", "passed": {"stop_id", "stop_name", "stop_lat", "stop_lon"}.issubset(stops.columns), "message": "outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv has required columns."})

if readable["t08_pois_clean"]:
    pois = pd.read_csv(outputs["t08_pois_clean"])
    checks.append({"check_name": "t08_pois_clean_columns", "passed": {"qid", "label", "latitude", "longitude"}.issubset(pois.columns), "message": "outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv has required columns."})

if readable["t10_accessibility_scores"]:
    access = pd.read_csv(outputs["t10_accessibility_scores"])
    scores_ok = pd.to_numeric(access["accessibility_score"], errors="coerce").between(0, 1).all()
    checks.append({"check_name": "t10_accessibility_scores_range", "passed": bool(scores_ok), "message": "outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv scores are bounded."})

if readable["t13_city_clusters"]:
    clusters = pd.read_csv(outputs["t13_city_clusters"])
    matrix = pd.read_csv(root / "outputs" / "t12_selected_matrix.csv")
    checks.append({"check_name": "t13_city_clusters_rows", "passed": len(clusters) == len(matrix), "message": "outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv covers selected matrix rows."})

(root / "outputs" / "t14_validation_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(checks, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

{"path":"src/t15_build_report.py","content":""""T15 - Build the reproducible validation report and the two result figures.

All numbers written into reports/pipeline_report.md are computed from the
pipeline artifacts in outputs/ at run time, so the report cannot drift away
from the data it describes. The script uses only local files (no network or
live API calls) and is deterministic apart from the run timestamp.

Run from the workspace root:

    python src/t15_build_report.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")  # headless rendering, no display / no network
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(".")
OUT = ROOT / "outputs"
FIG = ROOT / "figures"
REP = ROOT / "reports"

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "figure.dpi": 110,
        "savefig.dpi": 110,
        "font.size": 10,
        "axes.spines.top": False,
        "axes.spines.right": False,
        "axes.grid": True,
        "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    }
)


def load_csv(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_csv(OUT / name)


def load_json(name: str):
    return json.loads((OUT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def fmt_int(value) -> str:
    return f"{int(value):,}"


def fmt_float(value, digits: int = 3) -> str:
    return f"{float(value):.{digits}f}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load every artifact used by the report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
selected = load_csv("t01_selected_indicators.csv")
eurostat_raw = load_csv("t02_eurostat_raw.csv")
catalog = load_csv("t03_mobility_catalog.csv")
gtfs_summary = load_json("t04_gtfs_summary.json")
cleaning_report = load_json("t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json")
clean_stops = load_csv("t05_clean_stops.csv")
clean_stop_times = load_csv("t05_clean_stop_times.csv")
service = load_csv("t06_stop_service_intensity.csv")
pois = load_csv("t08_pois_clean.csv")
nearest = load_csv("t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv")
access = load_csv("t10_accessibility_scores.csv")
matrix = load_csv("t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv")
missing = load_csv("t12_missingness_report.csv")
selected_matrix = load_csv("t12_selected_matrix.csv")
clusters = load_csv("t13_city_clusters.csv")
profiles = load_csv("t13_cluster_profiles.csv")
validation = load_json("t14_validation_summary.json")

sparql_query = (OUT / "t07_query.sparql").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Derived facts (single source of truth for the narrative)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_selected = len(selected)
n_raw_rows = len(eurostat_raw)
n_raw_cities = eurostat_raw["city_id"].nunique()
n_raw_years = eurostat_raw["year"].nunique()

n_stops_raw = gtfs_summary.get("n_stops")
n_stops_clean = len(clean_stops)
n_stop_times_clean = len(clean_stop_times)
n_trips = gtfs_summary.get("n_trips")
n_routes = gtfs_summary.get("n_routes")

n_pois = len(pois)
poi_type_counts = pois["poi_type"].value_counts().sort_values(ascending=False)
n_clusters = int(profiles["cluster_id"].nunique())

n_matrix_rows = len(matrix)
n_matrix_cells = len(matrix) * (matrix.shape[1] - 3)

n_selected_matrix_rows = len(selected_matrix)
n_selected_non_missing = int(selected_matrix["DE1001V"].notna().sum())
n_cities_selected = selected_matrix["city_id"].nunique()
kept_indicators = missing.loc[missing["kept"].astype(bool), "indicator"].tolist()
dropped_indicators = missing.loc[~missing["kept"].astype(bool), "indicator"].tolist()

acc = access["accessibility_score"]
acc_by_type = (
    access.groupby("poi_type")["accessibility_score"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "median", "min", "max"])
    .sort_values("mean", ascending=False)
)
acc_median = float(acc.median())
acc_mean = float(acc.mean())
acc_min = float(acc.min())
acc_max = float(acc.max())
acc_q1 = float(acc.quantile(0.25))
acc_q3 = float(acc.quantile(0.75))
n_acc_ge_07 = int((acc >= 0.7).sum())
n_acc_lt_04 = int((acc < 0.4).sum())
best = access.loc[acc.idxmax()]
worst = access.loc[acc.idxmin()]
dist = access["distance_m"]

cluster_sizes = clusters["cluster_id"].value_counts().sort_index()
cluster_countries = (
    clusters.groupby("cluster_id")["city_id"]
    .apply(lambda s: sorted({c[:2] for c in s}))
    .to_dict()
)
cluster_is_country_row = (
    clusters.assign(is_country=clusters["city_id"].str.len() == 2)
    .groupby("cluster_id")["is_country"]
    .sum()
    .astype(int)
    .to_dict()
)
profile_cols = [c for c in profiles.columns if c != "cluster_id"]
profile_mean_col = profile_cols[0]
profile_values = profiles.set_index("cluster_id")[profile_mean_col]

validation_passed = sum(1 for c in validation if c["passed"])
validation_total = len(validation)
validation_all_ok = validation_passed == validation_total

n_service_stops = len(service)
median_departures = float(service["n_departures"].median())
max_departures = int(service["n_departures"].max())
single_departure_stops = int((service["n_departures"] == 1).sum())

generated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Figure 1 - distribution of POI accessibility scores
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4))

bins = [i / 20 for i in range(21)]
axes[0].hist(acc, bins=bins, color="#2f6f9f", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.6)
axes[0].axvline(acc_median, color="#c0392b", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.6,
                label=f"median = {acc_median:.3f}")
axes[0].set_title("Accessibility score distribution")
axes[0].set_xlabel("accessibility_score (0-1)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("number of POIs")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
axes[0].set_xlim(0, 1)

order = acc_by_type.index.tolist()
data = [access.loc[access["poi_type"] == t, "accessibility_score"].values for t in order]
axes[1].boxplot(data, labels=order, showmeans=True, widths=0.55,
                medianprops={"color": "#c0392b"}, meanprops={"marker": "o",
                "markerfacecolor": "#2f6f9f", "markeredgecolor": "#2f6f9f", "markersize": 4})
for i, t in enumerate(order, start=1):
    n_t = int((access["poi_type"] == t).sum())
    axes[1].annotate(f"n={n_t}", (i, 0.04), ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#444444")
axes[1].set_title("Scores by POI type (box = IQR, dot = mean)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("accessibility_score (0-1)")
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 1)
axes[1].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=20)
for lbl in axes[1].get_xticklabels():
    lbl.set_horizontalalignment("right")

fig.suptitle(
    f"Figure 1 - POI accessibility from outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv "
    f"(n={n_pois} POIs)",
    fontsize=11,
)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG / "fig_accessibility_distribution.png", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Figure 2 - cluster sizes and cluster profiles
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4))

cluster_ids = [int(c) for c in cluster_sizes.index]
sizes = [int(cluster_sizes.loc[c]) for c in cluster_ids]
bars = axes[0].bar([f"cluster {c}" for c in cluster_ids], sizes,
                   color="#4c8c5a", edgecolor="white")
axes[0].set_yscale("log")
axes[0].set_title(f"Cluster sizes (log scale), {n_clusters} clusters")
axes[0].set_ylabel("rows (city x year)")
for rect, value in zip(bars, sizes):
    axes[0].annotate(fmt_int(value), (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, value),
                     ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)
axes[0].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=15)

prof_vals = [float(profile_values.loc[c]) for c in cluster_ids]
bars = axes[1].bar([f"cluster {c}" for c in cluster_ids], prof_vals,
                   color="#8e5b9f", edgecolor="white")
axes[1].set_title(f"Cluster profile: mean {profile_mean_col} (population, 1 Jan)")
axes[1].set_ylabel(f"mean {profile_mean_col}")
axes[1].ticklabel_format(axis="y", style="sci", scilimits=(0, 0))
for rect, value in zip(bars, prof_vals):
    axes[1].annotate(f"{value:,.0f}",
                     (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, value),
                     ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)
axes[1].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=15)

fig.suptitle(
    "Figure 2 - Cluster structure from outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv and "
    "outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv",
    fontsize=11,
)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG / "fig_cluster_profiles.png", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
REP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

type_mean_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {t} | {int(r['count'])} | {r['mean']:.3f} | {r['median']:.3f} | "
    f"{r['min']:.3f} | {r['max']:.3f} |"
    for t, r in acc_by_type.iterrows()
)

missing_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {r.indicator} | {fmt_int(r.missing_count)} | {r.missing_rate:.3f} | "
    f"{'kept' if r.kept else 'dropped'} |"
    for r in missing.itertuples()
)

poi_type_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {t} | {fmt_int(c)} |" for t, c in poi_type_counts.items()
)

cluster_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {c} | {fmt_int(cluster_sizes.loc[c])} | "
    f"{profile_values.loc[c]:,.0f} | "
    f"{cluster_is_country_row.get(int(c), 0)} | "
    f"{', '.join(cluster_countries.get(int(c), []))} |"
    for c in cluster_ids
)

artifact_lines = "\n".join(
    [
        f"| `outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv` | {n_selected} selected urban indicators with theme and expected direction |",
        f"| `outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv` | {fmt_int(n_raw_rows)} raw Eurostat-style indicator rows covering {n_raw_cities} city IDs and {n_raw_years} distinct years |",
        f"| `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv` | {len(catalog)} catalog record(s) describing the public-transport data source |",
        f"| `outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` | GTFS archive summary: {n_stops_raw} stops, {n_routes} routes, {n_trips} trips, {gtfs_summary.get('n_stop_times')} stop_times rows |",
        f"| `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv` | {fmt_int(n_stops_clean)} stops retained after coordinate, duplicate and name cleaning |",
        f"| `outputs/t05_clean_stop_times.csv` | {fmt_int(n_stop_times_clean)} cleaned stop_times rows used for service intensity |",
        "| `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json` | counts of removed invalid coordinates, duplicates and filled names |",
        f"| `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv` | departures and route counts per stop for {fmt_int(n_service_stops)} stops |",
        "| `outputs/t07_query.sparql` | SPARQL query text used to define the POI extraction (documentation only) |",
        f"| `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv` | {n_pois} POIs with coordinates from the Wikidata snapshot |",
        f"| `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv` | nearest-stop join for {len(nearest)} POIs with distance in metres |",
        f"| `outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` | final accessibility score in [0, 1] for {n_pois} POIs |",
        f"| `outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv` | wide city-year matrix with {fmt_int(n_matrix_rows)} rows and {n_matrix_cells} indicator cells |",
        "| `outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv` | per-indicator missing counts, missing rates and keep/drop decisions |",
        f"| `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` | filtered matrix for the {len(kept_indicators)} kept indicator(s), {fmt_int(n_selected_matrix_rows)} rows |",
        f"| `outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv` | cluster label per city-year row ({fmt_int(len(clusters))} rows, {n_clusters} clusters) |",
        f"| `outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv` | mean indicator value for each of the {n_clusters} clusters |",
        f"| `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` | {validation_total} structural validation checks, {validation_passed} passed |",
        "| `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` | Figure 1, distribution of POI accessibility scores |",
        "| `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` | Figure 2, cluster sizes and cluster profile means |",
    ]
)

report = f"""# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under
`outputs/`. It summarises how the input samples were selected, cleaned, joined and
aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting
accessibility scores and city clusters show.

The pipeline combines three independent data views: Eurostat-style city indicators
(`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`), a static public-transport GTFS snapshot
(`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`) and a Wikidata POI
snapshot (`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`). Their join yields per-POI accessibility
scores (`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`), while the indicator matrix is
filtered for missingness (`outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`) and clustered
(`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`).

# Input data

All inputs live in `inputs/` and were read from disk; no request is issued to any
remote service at run time. The Eurostat component is a fixed snapshot described by
`inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json` (`"source": "eurostat_snapshot"`), with the
values stored in `inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv`, the indicator
labels in `inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv` and the table metadata in
`inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv`.

The mobility component consists of `inputs/catalog/dataeuropa_mobility_catalog_sample.json`
(one selected catalog record, written to `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`) and the
GTFS archive `inputs/gtfs/sample_city_gtfs.zip`, which is summarised in
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` with {n_stops_raw} stops, {n_routes} routes,
{n_trips} trips and {gtfs_summary.get('n_stop_times')} stop_times rows.

The POI component uses `inputs/wikidata/city_config.json` (city Alicante, QID Q11959,
five POI types) and the query result snapshot
`inputs/wikidata/wikidata_pois_sample.json`, which provides the {n_pois} geolocated
points of interest used downstream.

# Methods

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing {n_selected} candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`; indicators above the missing-rate threshold are
dropped, which leaves {len(kept_indicators)} indicator(s) ({', '.join(kept_indicators) or 'none'})
in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
are counted per stop in `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`.

POIs are extracted with the documented query in `outputs/t07_query.sparql`, cleaned
in `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, and matched to their nearest stop by haversine
distance in `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`. The accessibility score in
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` is a bounded [0, 1] combination of proximity
(shorter distance is better) and service intensity (more departures and routes are
better), and is explicitly validated to stay within that range.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

# Generated outputs

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
{artifact_lines}

Reproduce this report and both figures from the workspace root with
`python src/t15_build_report.py` after the upstream pipeline steps and
`python src/validate_outputs.py` have completed. Every figure caption and every
number quoted below is read from the files listed in this table at build time.

# Main results

**Accessibility.** Across the {n_pois} POIs the accessibility score has a mean of
{fmt_float(acc_mean)} and a median of {fmt_float(acc_median)}, an interquartile range
of {fmt_float(acc_q1)} to {fmt_float(acc_q3)}, and spans {fmt_float(acc_min)} to
{fmt_float(acc_max)}. {n_acc_ge_07} POIs reach at least 0.70 while {n_acc_lt_04}
fall below 0.40. The highest score belongs to "{best['label']}"
({fmt_float(best['accessibility_score'])}, {fmt_float(best['distance_m'], 1)} m from
its nearest stop) and the lowest to "{worst['label']}"
({fmt_float(worst['accessibility_score'])}, {fmt_float(worst['distance_m'], 1)} m).

| POI type | POIs | mean score | median score | min | max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
{type_mean_lines}

Nearest-stop distances range from {fmt_float(dist.min(), 1)} m to
{fmt_float(dist.max(), 1)} m with a median of {fmt_float(dist.median(), 1)} m, so the
score variation is driven mainly by how far a POI sits from any served stop.

**Service supply.** {fmt_int(single_departure_stops)} of the {fmt_int(n_service_stops)}
clean stops ({single_departure_stops / n_service_stops:.1%}) have a single recorded
departure in the GTFS snapshot, the median stop has
{fmt_float(median_departures, 1)} departures and the busiest stop has
{max_departures}. This is a thin snapshot, which limits how far the accessibility
scores can be generalised.

**Indicator matrix and missingness.**

| Indicator | Missing rows | Missing rate | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
{missing_lines}

After filtering, `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` keeps {fmt_int(n_selected_matrix_rows)}
city-year rows and {fmt_int(n_selected_non_missing)} non-missing
{', '.join(kept_indicators) or ''} values across {fmt_int(n_cities_selected)} city IDs.

**Clusters.**

| Cluster | Rows | Mean {profile_mean_col} | Country-level rows | Countries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
{cluster_lines}

The clustering is strongly imbalanced: cluster 0 holds {fmt_int(cluster_sizes.loc[0])}
of {fmt_int(len(clusters))} rows, while clusters 1 and 2 contain
{fmt_int(cluster_sizes.sum() - cluster_sizes.loc[0])} rows in total. Because the
selected indicator is an absolute population count, the dominant split separates
very large national aggregates from individual cities rather than distinguishing
cities with similar density profiles.

**Validation.** `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` reports {validation_passed} of
{validation_total} checks passing, and that file is the machine-readable record of the
run's structural integrity; see `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` for the
score distribution and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` for the cluster structure.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: {n_pois} POIs, {fmt_int(n_service_stops)} clean stops and
{fmt_int(n_selected_matrix_rows)} city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
a live or authoritative measurement of any real city.

Only {len(kept_indicators)} of the {n_selected} selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping {', '.join(dropped_indicators) or 'none'}; the modal-split
and household indicators that would best capture livability were therefore unavailable,
and the remaining analysis rests on a single absolute population count.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, which is why clusters 1 and 2 consist almost entirely of
country-level rows. Cluster membership should not be interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. No live
Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata API is contacted at any point, and the pipeline
deliberately makes no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files.

`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`. Report built on {generated_at} from offline
snapshot files only, with no live API access.
"""

args.content:
"""T15 - Build the reproducible validation report and the two result figures.

All numbers written into reports/pipeline_report.md are computed from the
pipeline artifacts in outputs/ at run time, so the report cannot drift away
from the data it describes. The script uses only local files (no network or
live API calls) and is deterministic apart from the run timestamp.

Run from the workspace root:

    python src/t15_build_report.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")  # headless rendering, no display / no network
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(".")
OUT = ROOT / "outputs"
FIG = ROOT / "figures"
REP = ROOT / "reports"

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "figure.dpi": 110,
        "savefig.dpi": 110,
        "font.size": 10,
        "axes.spines.top": False,
        "axes.spines.right": False,
        "axes.grid": True,
        "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    }
)


def load_csv(name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_csv(OUT / name)


def load_json(name: str):
    return json.loads((OUT / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def fmt_int(value) -> str:
    return f"{int(value):,}"


def fmt_float(value, digits: int = 3) -> str:
    return f"{float(value):.{digits}f}"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load every artifact used by the report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
selected = load_csv("t01_selected_indicators.csv")
eurostat_raw = load_csv("t02_eurostat_raw.csv")
catalog = load_csv("t03_mobility_catalog.csv")
gtfs_summary = load_json("t04_gtfs_summary.json")
cleaning_report = load_json("t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json")
clean_stops = load_csv("t05_clean_stops.csv")
clean_stop_times = load_csv("t05_clean_stop_times.csv")
service = load_csv("t06_stop_service_intensity.csv")
pois = load_csv("t08_pois_clean.csv")
nearest = load_csv("t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv")
access = load_csv("t10_accessibility_scores.csv")
matrix = load_csv("t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv")
missing = load_csv("t12_missingness_report.csv")
selected_matrix = load_csv("t12_selected_matrix.csv")
clusters = load_csv("t13_city_clusters.csv")
profiles = load_csv("t13_cluster_profiles.csv")
validation = load_json("t14_validation_summary.json")

sparql_query = (OUT / "t07_query.sparql").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Derived facts (single source of truth for the narrative)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_selected = len(selected)
n_raw_rows = len(eurostat_raw)
n_raw_cities = eurostat_raw["city_id"].nunique()
n_raw_years = eurostat_raw["year"].nunique()

n_stops_raw = gtfs_summary.get("n_stops")
n_stops_clean = len(clean_stops)
n_stop_times_clean = len(clean_stop_times)
n_trips = gtfs_summary.get("n_trips")
n_routes = gtfs_summary.get("n_routes")

n_pois = len(pois)
poi_type_counts = pois["poi_type"].value_counts().sort_values(ascending=False)
n_clusters = int(profiles["cluster_id"].nunique())

n_matrix_rows = len(matrix)
n_matrix_cells = len(matrix) * (matrix.shape[1] - 3)

n_selected_matrix_rows = len(selected_matrix)
n_selected_non_missing = int(selected_matrix["DE1001V"].notna().sum())
n_cities_selected = selected_matrix["city_id"].nunique()
kept_indicators = missing.loc[missing["kept"].astype(bool), "indicator"].tolist()
dropped_indicators = missing.loc[~missing["kept"].astype(bool), "indicator"].tolist()

acc = access["accessibility_score"]
acc_by_type = (
    access.groupby("poi_type")["accessibility_score"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "median", "min", "max"])
    .sort_values("mean", ascending=False)
)
acc_median = float(acc.median())
acc_mean = float(acc.mean())
acc_min = float(acc.min())
acc_max = float(acc.max())
acc_q1 = float(acc.quantile(0.25))
acc_q3 = float(acc.quantile(0.75))
n_acc_ge_07 = int((acc >= 0.7).sum())
n_acc_lt_04 = int((acc < 0.4).sum())
best = access.loc[acc.idxmax()]
worst = access.loc[acc.idxmin()]
dist = access["distance_m"]

cluster_sizes = clusters["cluster_id"].value_counts().sort_index()
cluster_countries = (
    clusters.groupby("cluster_id")["city_id"]
    .apply(lambda s: sorted({c[:2] for c in s}))
    .to_dict()
)
cluster_is_country_row = (
    clusters.assign(is_country=clusters["city_id"].str.len() == 2)
    .groupby("cluster_id")["is_country"]
    .sum()
    .astype(int)
    .to_dict()
)
profile_cols = [c for c in profiles.columns if c != "cluster_id"]
profile_mean_col = profile_cols[0]
profile_values = profiles.set_index("cluster_id")[profile_mean_col]

validation_passed = sum(1 for c in validation if c["passed"])
validation_total = len(validation)
validation_all_ok = validation_passed == validation_total

n_service_stops = len(service)
median_departures = float(service["n_departures"].median())
max_departures = int(service["n_departures"].max())
single_departure_stops = int((service["n_departures"] == 1).sum())

generated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Figure 1 - distribution of POI accessibility scores
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4))

bins = [i / 20 for i in range(21)]
axes[0].hist(acc, bins=bins, color="#2f6f9f", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.6)
axes[0].axvline(acc_median, color="#c0392b", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.6,
                label=f"median = {acc_median:.3f}")
axes[0].set_title("Accessibility score distribution")
axes[0].set_xlabel("accessibility_score (0-1)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("number of POIs")
axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9)
axes[0].set_xlim(0, 1)

order = acc_by_type.index.tolist()
data = [access.loc[access["poi_type"] == t, "accessibility_score"].values for t in order]
axes[1].boxplot(data, labels=order, showmeans=True, widths=0.55,
                medianprops={"color": "#c0392b"}, meanprops={"marker": "o",
                "markerfacecolor": "#2f6f9f", "markeredgecolor": "#2f6f9f", "markersize": 4})
for i, t in enumerate(order, start=1):
    n_t = int((access["poi_type"] == t).sum())
    axes[1].annotate(f"n={n_t}", (i, 0.04), ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#444444")
axes[1].set_title("Scores by POI type (box = IQR, dot = mean)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("accessibility_score (0-1)")
axes[1].set_ylim(0, 1)
axes[1].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=20)
for lbl in axes[1].get_xticklabels():
    lbl.set_horizontalalignment("right")

fig.suptitle(
    f"Figure 1 - POI accessibility from outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv "
    f"(n={n_pois} POIs)",
    fontsize=11,
)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG / "fig_accessibility_distribution.png", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Figure 2 - cluster sizes and cluster profiles
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.4))

cluster_ids = [int(c) for c in cluster_sizes.index]
sizes = [int(cluster_sizes.loc[c]) for c in cluster_ids]
bars = axes[0].bar([f"cluster {c}" for c in cluster_ids], sizes,
                   color="#4c8c5a", edgecolor="white")
axes[0].set_yscale("log")
axes[0].set_title(f"Cluster sizes (log scale), {n_clusters} clusters")
axes[0].set_ylabel("rows (city x year)")
for rect, value in zip(bars, sizes):
    axes[0].annotate(fmt_int(value), (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, value),
                     ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)
axes[0].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=15)

prof_vals = [float(profile_values.loc[c]) for c in cluster_ids]
bars = axes[1].bar([f"cluster {c}" for c in cluster_ids], prof_vals,
                   color="#8e5b9f", edgecolor="white")
axes[1].set_title(f"Cluster profile: mean {profile_mean_col} (population, 1 Jan)")
axes[1].set_ylabel(f"mean {profile_mean_col}")
axes[1].ticklabel_format(axis="y", style="sci", scilimits=(0, 0))
for rect, value in zip(bars, prof_vals):
    axes[1].annotate(f"{value:,.0f}",
                     (rect.get_x() + rect.get_width() / 2, value),
                     ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)
axes[1].tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=15)

fig.suptitle(
    "Figure 2 - Cluster structure from outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv and "
    "outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv",
    fontsize=11,
)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG / "fig_cluster_profiles.png", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
REP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

type_mean_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {t} | {int(r['count'])} | {r['mean']:.3f} | {r['median']:.3f} | "
    f"{r['min']:.3f} | {r['max']:.3f} |"
    for t, r in acc_by_type.iterrows()
)

missing_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {r.indicator} | {fmt_int(r.missing_count)} | {r.missing_rate:.3f} | "
    f"{'kept' if r.kept else 'dropped'} |"
    for r in missing.itertuples()
)

poi_type_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {t} | {fmt_int(c)} |" for t, c in poi_type_counts.items()
)

cluster_lines = "\n".join(
    f"| {c} | {fmt_int(cluster_sizes.loc[c])} | "
    f"{profile_values.loc[c]:,.0f} | "
    f"{cluster_is_country_row.get(int(c), 0)} | "
    f"{', '.join(cluster_countries.get(int(c), []))} |"
    for c in cluster_ids
)

artifact_lines = "\n".join(
    [
        f"| `outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv` | {n_selected} selected urban indicators with theme and expected direction |",
        f"| `outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv` | {fmt_int(n_raw_rows)} raw Eurostat-style indicator rows covering {n_raw_cities} city IDs and {n_raw_years} distinct years |",
        f"| `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv` | {len(catalog)} catalog record(s) describing the public-transport data source |",
        f"| `outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` | GTFS archive summary: {n_stops_raw} stops, {n_routes} routes, {n_trips} trips, {gtfs_summary.get('n_stop_times')} stop_times rows |",
        f"| `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv` | {fmt_int(n_stops_clean)} stops retained after coordinate, duplicate and name cleaning |",
        f"| `outputs/t05_clean_stop_times.csv` | {fmt_int(n_stop_times_clean)} cleaned stop_times rows used for service intensity |",
        "| `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json` | counts of removed invalid coordinates, duplicates and filled names |",
        f"| `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv` | departures and route counts per stop for {fmt_int(n_service_stops)} stops |",
        "| `outputs/t07_query.sparql` | SPARQL query text used to define the POI extraction (documentation only) |",
        f"| `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv` | {n_pois} POIs with coordinates from the Wikidata snapshot |",
        f"| `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv` | nearest-stop join for {len(nearest)} POIs with distance in metres |",
        f"| `outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` | final accessibility score in [0, 1] for {n_pois} POIs |",
        f"| `outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv` | wide city-year matrix with {fmt_int(n_matrix_rows)} rows and {n_matrix_cells} indicator cells |",
        "| `outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv` | per-indicator missing counts, missing rates and keep/drop decisions |",
        f"| `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` | filtered matrix for the {len(kept_indicators)} kept indicator(s), {fmt_int(n_selected_matrix_rows)} rows |",
        f"| `outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv` | cluster label per city-year row ({fmt_int(len(clusters))} rows, {n_clusters} clusters) |",
        f"| `outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv` | mean indicator value for each of the {n_clusters} clusters |",
        f"| `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` | {validation_total} structural validation checks, {validation_passed} passed |",
        "| `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` | Figure 1, distribution of POI accessibility scores |",
        "| `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` | Figure 2, cluster sizes and cluster profile means |",
    ]
)

report = f"""# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under

aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting

# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under
`outputs/`. It summarises how the input samples were selected, cleaned, joined and
aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting
accessibility scores and city clusters show.

The pipeline combines three independent data views: Eurostat-style city indicators
(`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`), a static public-transport GTFS snapshot
(`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`) and a Wikidata POI
snapshot (`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`). Their join yields per-POI accessibility
scores (`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`), while the indicator matrix is
filtered for missingness (`outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`) and clustered
(`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`).

# Input data

All inputs live in `inputs/` and were read from disk; no request is issued to any
remote service at run time. The Eurostat component is a fixed snapshot described by
`inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json` (`"source": "eurostat_snapshot"`), with the
values stored in `inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv`, the indicator
labels in `inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv` and the table metadata in
`inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv`.

The mobility component consists of `inputs/catalog/dataeuropa_mobility_catalog_sample.json`
(one selected catalog record, written to `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`) and the
GTFS archive `inputs/gtfs/sample_city_gtfs.zip`, which is summarised in
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` with 409 stops, 25 routes,
80 trips and 1893 stop_times rows.

The POI component uses `inputs/wikidata/city_config.json` (city Alicante, QID Q11959,
five POI types) and the query result snapshot
`inputs/wikidata/wikidata_pois_sample.json`, which provides the 48 geolocated
points of interest used downstream.

# Methods

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing 12 candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`; indicators above the missing-rate threshold are
dropped, which leaves 1 indicator(s) (DE1001V)
in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
are counted per stop in `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`.

POIs are extracted with the documented query in `outputs/t07_query.sparql`, cleaned
in `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, and matched to their nearest stop by haversine
distance in `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`. The accessibility score in
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` is a bounded [0, 1] combination of proximity
(shorter distance is better) and service intensity (more departures and routes are
better), and is explicitly validated to stay within that range.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

# Generated outputs

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv` | 12 selected urban indicators with theme and expected direction |
| `outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv` | 3,120 raw Eurostat-style indicator rows covering 686 city IDs and 4 distinct years |
| `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv` | 1 catalog record(s) describing the public-transport data source |
| `outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` | GTFS archive summary: 409 stops, 25 routes, 80 trips, 1893 stop_times rows |
| `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv` | 407 stops retained after coordinate, duplicate and name cleaning |
| `outputs/t05_clean_stop_times.csv` | 1,892 cleaned stop_times rows used for service intensity |
| `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json` | counts of removed invalid coordinates, duplicates and filled names |
| `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv` | departures and route counts per stop for 407 stops |
| `outputs/t07_query.sparql` | SPARQL query text used to define the POI extraction (documentation only) |
| `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv` | 48 POIs with coordinates from the Wikidata snapshot |
| `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv` | nearest-stop join for 48 POIs with distance in metres |
| `outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` | final accessibility score in [0, 1] for 48 POIs |
| `outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv` | wide city-year matrix with 1,612 rows and 12896 indicator cells |

number quoted below is read from the files listed in this table at build time.

# Main results

**Accessibility.** Across the 48 POIs the accessibility score has a mean of
0.598 and a median of 0.637, an interquartile range
of 0.521 to 0.725, and spans 0.142 to
0.865. 15 POIs reach at least 0.70 while 5
fall below 0.40. The highest score belongs to "Monumento al foguerer"
(0.865, 34.0 m from
its nearest stop) and the lowest to "Torre del Cabo de las Huertas"
(0.142, 1285.7 m).

| POI type | POIs | mean score | median score | min | max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| theatre building | 2 | 0.777 | 0.777 | 0.770 | 0.785 |
| art gallery | 1 | 0.708 | 0.708 | 0.708 | 0.708 |
| library | 13 | 0.631 | 0.638 | 0.316 | 0.814 |
| museum | 4 | 0.606 | 0.617 | 0.425 | 0.765 |
| monument | 28 | 0.565 | 0.590 | 0.142 | 0.865 |

Nearest-stop distances range from 29.6 m to
4222.8 m with a median of 207.3 m, so the
score variation is driven mainly by how far a POI sits from any served stop.

**Service supply.** 104 of the 407
clean stops (25.6%) have a single recorded
departure in the GTFS snapshot, the median stop has
3.0 departures and the busiest stop has
24. This is a thin snapshot, which limits how far the accessibility
scores can be generalised.

**Indicator matrix and missingness.**

| Indicator | Missing rows | Missing rate | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DE1001V | 454 | 0.282 | kept |
| DE1002V | 1,270 | 0.788 | dropped |
| DE3001V | 805 | 0.499 | dropped |
| DE3017V | 919 | 0.570 | dropped |
| TT1003V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1006V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1007V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1010V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |

After filtering, `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` keeps 1,612
city-year rows and 1,158 non-missing
DE1001V values across 686 city IDs.

**Clusters.**

| Cluster | Rows | Mean DE1001V | Country-level rows | Countries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1,598 | 246,135 | 9 | BE, BG, CH, DE, EE, ES, FI, FR, HR, HU, IT, LT, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, SE, SI |
| 1 | 4 | 53,637,101 | 4 | IT, PL |
| 2 | 10 | 12,283,182 | 10 | BE, NL, PT, SE |

The clustering is strongly imbalanced: cluster 0 holds 1,598
of 1,612 rows, while clusters 1 and 2 contain
14 rows in total. Because the
selected indicator is an absolute population count, the dominant split separates
very large national aggregates from individual cities rather than distinguishing
cities with similar density profiles.

**Validation.** `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` reports 9 of
9 checks passing, and that file is the machine-readable record of the
run's structural integrity; see `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` for the
score distribution and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` for the cluster structure.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: 48 POIs, 407 clean stops and
1,612 city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
a live or authoritative measurement of any real city.

Only 1 of the 12 selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping DE1002V, DE3001V, DE3017V, TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V; the modal-split
and household indicators that would best capture livability were therefore unavailable,
and the remaining analysis rests on a single absolute population count.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, which is why clusters 1 and 2 consist almost entirely of
country-level rows. Cluster membership should not be interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. No live
Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata API is contacted at any point, and the pipeline
deliberately makes no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: 48 POIs, 407 clean stops and
1,612 city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
a live or authoritative measurement of any real city.

Only 1 of the 12 selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping DE1002V, DE3001V, DE3017V, TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V; the modal-split
and household indicators that would best capture livability were therefore unavailable,
and the remaining analysis rests on a single absolute population count.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, which is why clusters 1 and 2 consist almost entirely of
country-level rows. Cluster membership should not be interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. The pipeline never
contacts Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata over the network at run time, and it makes
no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files described above.

reads only files under `outputs/`, uses a fixed random-free matplotlib Agg backend,

`figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png`
deterministically. Re-running it on the same artifacts reproduces identical figures
and identical narrative numbers, apart from the build timestamp.

# Methods

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing 12 candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`, where each indicator carries a `kept` flag
alongside its missing count and missing rate; only rows flagged `kept = True` are
carried forward, which leaves 1 indicator(s)
(DE1001V) in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
are counted per stop in `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`.

POIs are extracted with the documented query in `outputs/t07_query.sparql`, cleaned
in `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, and matched to their nearest stop by haversine
distance in `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`. The accessibility score in
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` is a bounded [0, 1] combination of proximity
(shorter distance is better) and service intensity (more departures and routes are
better), and is explicitly validated to stay within that range.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under
`outputs/`. It summarises how the input samples were selected, cleaned, joined and
aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting
accessibility scores and city clusters show.

The pipeline combines three independent data views: Eurostat-style city indicators
(`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`), a static public-transport GTFS snapshot
(`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`) and a Wikidata POI
snapshot (`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`). Their join yields per-POI accessibility
scores (`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`), while the indicator matrix is
filtered for missingness (`outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`) and clustered
(`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`).

# Input data

All inputs live in `inputs/` and were read from disk; no request is issued to any
remote service at run time. The Eurostat component is a fixed snapshot described by
`inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json` (`"source": "eurostat_snapshot"`), with the
values stored in `inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv`, the indicator
labels in `inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv` and the table metadata in
`inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv`.

The mobility component consists of `inputs/catalog/dataeuropa_mobility_catalog_sample.json`
(one selected catalog record, written to `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`) and the
GTFS archive `inputs/gtfs/sample_city_gtfs.zip`, which is summarised in
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` with 409 stops, 25 routes,
80 trips and 1893 stop_times rows.

The POI component uses `inputs/wikidata/city_config.json` (city Alicante, QID Q11959,
five POI types) and the query result snapshot
`inputs/wikidata/wikidata_pois_sample.json`, which provides the 48 geolocated
points of interest used downstream.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: 48 POIs, 407 clean stops and
1,612 city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
a live or authoritative measurement of any real city.

Only 1 of the 12 selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping DE1002V, DE3001V, DE3017V, TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V; the modal-split
and household indicators that would best capture livability were therefore unavailable,
and the remaining analysis rests on a single absolute population count.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, which is why clusters 1 and 2 consist almost entirely of
country-level rows. Cluster membership should not be interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. The pipeline never
contacts Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata over the network at run time, and it makes
no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files described above.

# Reproducibility

The report and both figures are generated by `python src/t15_build_report.py`, which
reads only files under `outputs/`, uses a fixed random-free matplotlib Agg backend,
and writes `reports/pipeline_report.md`,
`figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png`
deterministically. Re-running it on the same artifacts reproduces identical figures
and identical narrative numbers, apart from the build timestamp.

Ordered re-execution: build the indicators and raw matrix (`src/t02_load_eurostat.py`),
run the GTFS, POI and accessibility stages that emit `outputs/t05_*` through
`outputs/t10_*`, then clustering (`outputs/t13_*`), then validation
(`python src/validate_outputs.py` producing `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`),
and finally this reporting step. Validation status at build time:
9/9 checks passed (all green).

`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`, `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`,

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing 12 candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`, where each indicator carries a `kept` flag
alongside its missing count and missing rate; only rows flagged `kept = True` are
carried forward, which leaves 1 indicator
(DE1001V) in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
...
validation stage checks that no stored score falls outside that interval, and the
correlations reported under Main results show how strongly each component is reflected
in the stored values.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: 48 POIs, 407 clean stops and
1,612 city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
an authoritative, up-to-date measurement of any real city.

Only 1 of the 12 selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping DE1002V, DE3001V, DE3017V, TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V. All four
modal-split indicators (TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V) are missing in at least
98.1% of matrix rows, so the analysis rests on a single absolute population count
(DE1001V) rather than on the travel-behaviour indicators.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, so clusters 1 and 2 end up containing only country-level
rows while cluster 0 holds essentially all cities. Cluster membership should not be
interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. The pipeline never
contacts Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata over the network at run time, and it makes
no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files described above.

# Reproducibility

result.stdout:
# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under
`outputs/`. It summarises how the input samples were selected, cleaned, joined and
aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting
accessibility scores and city clusters show.

The pipeline combines three independent data views: Eurostat-style city indicators
(`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`), a static public-transport GTFS snapshot
(`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`) and a Wikidata POI
snapshot (`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`). Their join yields per-POI accessibility
scores (`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`), while the indicator matrix is
filtered for missingness (`outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`) and clustered
(`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`).

# Input data

All inputs reside in `inputs/` and are read from disk; no request is issued to any
remote service at run time. The Eurostat component is a fixed snapshot described by
`inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json` (`"source": "eurostat_snapshot"`), with the
values stored in `inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv`, the indicator
labels in `inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv` and the table metadata in
`inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv`.

The mobility component consists of `inputs/catalog/dataeuropa_mobility_catalog_sample.json`
(one selected catalog record, written to `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`) and the
GTFS archive `inputs/gtfs/sample_city_gtfs.zip`, which is summarised in
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` with 409 stops, 25 routes,
80 trips and 1893 stop_times rows.

The POI component uses `inputs/wikidata/city_config.json` (city Alicante, QID Q11959,
five POI types) and the query result snapshot
`inputs/wikidata/wikidata_pois_sample.json`, which provides the 48 geolocated
points of interest used downstream.

# Methods

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing 12 candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`, where each indicator carries a `kept` flag
alongside its missing count and missing rate; only rows flagged `kept = True` are
carried forward, which leaves 1 indicator
(DE1001V) in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
are counted per stop in `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`.

POIs are extracted with the documented query in `outputs/t07_query.sparql`, cleaned
in `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, and matched to their nearest stop by haversine
distance in `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`. The accessibility score in
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` is scaled to the interval [0, 1], where shorter
nearest-stop distance and higher departure and route counts both raise the score; the
validation stage checks that no stored score falls outside that interval, and the
correlations reported under Main results show how strongly each component is reflected
in the stored values.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

result.content:
# Overview

This report documents the reproducible urban mobility and livability pipeline that
runs entirely from fixed offline snapshots and produces the artifacts stored under
`outputs/`. It summarises how the input samples were selected, cleaned, joined and
aggregated, which outputs were generated in the workspace, and what the resulting
accessibility scores and city clusters show.

The pipeline combines three independent data views: Eurostat-style city indicators
(`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`), a static public-transport GTFS snapshot
(`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`) and a Wikidata POI
snapshot (`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`). Their join yields per-POI accessibility
scores (`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`), while the indicator matrix is
filtered for missingness (`outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`) and clustered
(`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`).

# Input data

All inputs reside in `inputs/` and are read from disk; no request is issued to any
remote service at run time. The Eurostat component is a fixed snapshot described by
`inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json` (`"source": "eurostat_snapshot"`), with the
values stored in `inputs/eurostat/eurostat_city_values_sample.csv`, the indicator
labels in `inputs/eurostat/indicator_descriptions.csv` and the table metadata in
`inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv`.

The mobility component consists of `inputs/catalog/dataeuropa_mobility_catalog_sample.json`
(one selected catalog record, written to `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`) and the
GTFS archive `inputs/gtfs/sample_city_gtfs.zip`, which is summarised in
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` with 409 stops, 25 routes,
80 trips and 1893 stop_times rows.

The POI component uses `inputs/wikidata/city_config.json` (city Alicante, QID Q11959,
five POI types) and the query result snapshot
`inputs/wikidata/wikidata_pois_sample.json`, which provides the 48 geolocated
points of interest used downstream.

# Methods

Indicator selection keeps only indicators whose theme, justification and expected
direction are documented, producing 12 candidates in
`outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`. The city indicator matrix
(`outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`) is then profiled for missingness in
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`, where each indicator carries a `kept` flag
alongside its missing count and missing rate; only rows flagged `kept = True` are
carried forward, which leaves 1 indicator
(DE1001V) in `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`.

The GTFS archive is parsed into stops and stop_times, then cleaned: invalid
coordinates, duplicate stops and blank stop names are handled and the counts are
recorded in `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`. Departures and distinct routes
are counted per stop in `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`.

POIs are extracted with the documented query in `outputs/t07_query.sparql`, cleaned
in `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, and matched to their nearest stop by haversine
distance in `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`. The accessibility score in
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` is scaled to the interval [0, 1], where shorter
nearest-stop distance and higher departure and route counts both raise the score; the
validation stage checks that no stored score falls outside that interval, and the
correlations reported under Main results show how strongly each component is reflected
in the stored values.

Clustering is performed on the filtered matrix and written to
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, with per-cluster means in
`outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv`. Structural checks on all of these files are
executed by `src/validate_outputs.py` and recorded in
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`.

# Generated outputs

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv` | 12 selected urban indicators with theme and expected direction |
| `outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv` | 3,120 raw Eurostat-style indicator rows covering 686 city IDs and 4 distinct years |
| `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv` | 1 catalog record describing the public-transport data source |
| `outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json` | GTFS archive summary: 409 stops, 25 routes, 80 trips, 1893 stop_times rows |
| `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv` | 407 stops retained after coordinate, duplicate and name cleaning |
| `outputs/t05_clean_stop_times.csv` | 1,892 cleaned stop_times rows used for service intensity |
| `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json` | counts of removed invalid coordinates, duplicates and filled names |
| `outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv` | departures and route counts per stop for 407 stops |
| `outputs/t07_query.sparql` | SPARQL query text used to define the POI extraction (documentation only) |
| `outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv` | 48 POIs with coordinates from the Wikidata snapshot |
| `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv` | nearest-stop join for 48 POIs with distance in metres |
| `outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` | final accessibility score in [0, 1] for 48 POIs |
| `outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv` | wide city-year matrix with 1,612 rows and 12,896 indicator cells |
| `outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv` | per-indicator missing counts, missing rates and keep/drop decisions |
| `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` | filtered matrix with 1 retained indicator over 1,612 city-year rows |
| `outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv` | cluster label per city-year row (1,612 rows, 3 clusters) |
| `outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv` | mean indicator value for each of the 3 clusters |
| `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` | 9 structural validation checks, 9 passed |
| `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` | Figure 1, distribution of POI accessibility scores |
| `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` | Figure 2, cluster sizes and cluster profile means |

Reproduce this report and both figures from the workspace root with
`python src/t15_build_report.py` after the upstream pipeline steps and
`python src/validate_outputs.py` have completed. Every figure caption and every
number quoted below is read from the files listed in this table at build time.

# Main results

**Accessibility.** Across the 48 POIs the accessibility score has a mean of
0.598 and a median of 0.637, an interquartile range
of 0.521 to 0.725, and spans 0.142 to
0.865. 15 POIs reach at least 0.70 while 5
fall below 0.40. The highest score belongs to "Monumento al foguerer"
(0.865, 34.0 m from
its nearest stop) and the lowest to "Torre del Cabo de las Huertas"
(0.142, 1285.7 m).

| POI type | POIs | mean score | median score | min | max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| theatre building | 2 | 0.777 | 0.777 | 0.770 | 0.785 |
| art gallery | 1 | 0.708 | 0.708 | 0.708 | 0.708 |
| library | 13 | 0.631 | 0.638 | 0.316 | 0.814 |
| museum | 4 | 0.606 | 0.617 | 0.425 | 0.765 |
| monument | 28 | 0.565 | 0.590 | 0.142 | 0.865 |

Nearest-stop distances range from 29.6 m to
4222.8 m with a median of 207.3 m. Within
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv` the Spearman correlation between distance and
score is -0.801 and between departure count and score it is
0.593, so distance is the dominant driver of the score and service
intensity acts as a secondary, weaker term.

**Service supply.** 104 of the 407
clean stops (25.6%) have a single recorded
departure in the GTFS snapshot, the median stop has
3.0 departures and the busiest stop has
24. This is a thin snapshot, which limits how far the accessibility
scores can be generalised.

**Indicator matrix and missingness.**

| Indicator | Missing rows | Missing rate | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DE1001V | 454 | 0.282 | kept |
| DE1002V | 1,270 | 0.788 | dropped |
| DE3001V | 805 | 0.499 | dropped |
| DE3017V | 919 | 0.570 | dropped |
| TT1003V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1006V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1007V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |
| TT1010V | 1,582 | 0.981 | dropped |

After filtering, `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv` keeps 1,612
city-year rows spanning 686 distinct city IDs, of which
1,158 carry a non-missing DE1001V
value (71.8% coverage).

**Clusters.**

| Cluster | Rows | Mean DE1001V | Country-level rows | Countries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1,598 | 246,135 | 9 | BE, BG, CH, DE, EE, ES, FI, FR, HR, HU, IT, LT, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, SE, SI |
| 1 | 4 | 53,637,101 | 4 | IT, PL |
| 2 | 10 | 12,283,182 | 10 | BE, NL, PT, SE |

Every row in clusters 1 and 2 is a two-letter national aggregate row
(4 of 4 in cluster 1
and 10 of 10 in
cluster 2, for example `IT`, `PL`, `BE`, `NL`, `PT`, `SE`), while only
9 of the 1,598 cluster-0
rows are country aggregates and the rest are individual cities.

The clustering is strongly imbalanced: cluster 0 holds 1,598
of 1,612 rows, while clusters 1 and 2 contain
14 rows in total. Because the
selected indicator is an absolute population count, the dominant split separates
very large national aggregates from individual cities rather than distinguishing
cities with similar density profiles.

**Validation.** `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json` reports 9 of
9 checks passing, and that file is the machine-readable record of the
run's structural integrity; see `figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` for the
score distribution and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png` for the cluster structure.

# Limitations

The three components are small offline snapshots rather than full population
datasets: 48 POIs, 407 clean stops and
1,612 city-year rows, so no result here should be read as
an authoritative, up-to-date measurement of any real city.

Only 1 of the 12 selected indicators survived the
missingness filter, dropping DE1002V, DE3001V, DE3017V, TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V. All four
modal-split indicators (TT1003V, TT1006V, TT1007V, TT1010V) are missing in at least
98.1% of matrix rows, so the analysis rests on a single absolute population count
(DE1001V) rather than on the travel-behaviour indicators.

The clustering inherits two further weaknesses: it operates on one unstandardised
variable, so absolute scale dominates the grouping, and it mixes national aggregate
rows with individual cities, so clusters 1 and 2 end up containing only country-level
rows while cluster 0 holds essentially all cities. Cluster membership should not be
interpreted as an urban typology.

Accessibility scores depend on a nearest-stop join with straight-line distances and
on GTFS departure counts from a single snapshot; they ignore walking-network
topology, service frequency by time of day, crowding and modal quality. The pipeline never
contacts Eurostat, data.europa.eu or Wikidata over the network at run time, and it makes
no claim about data freshness beyond the archived snapshot files described above.

# Reproducibility

The report and both figures are generated by `python src/t15_build_report.py`, which
reads only files under `outputs/`, uses a fixed random-free matplotlib Agg backend,
and writes `reports/pipeline_report.md`,
`figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png` and `figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png`
deterministically. Re-running it on the same artifacts reproduces identical figures
and identical narrative numbers, apart from the build timestamp.

Ordered re-execution: build the indicators and raw matrix (`src/t02_load_eurostat.py`),
run the GTFS, POI and accessibility stages that emit `outputs/t05_*` through
`outputs/t10_*`, then clustering (`outputs/t13_*`), then validation
(`python src/validate_outputs.py` producing `outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`),
and finally this reporting step. Validation status at build time:
9/9 checks passed (all green).

Artifacts of this run: `outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv`,
`outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv`, `outputs/t03_mobility_catalog.csv`,
`outputs/t04_gtfs_summary.json`, `outputs/t05_clean_stops.csv`,
`outputs/t05_clean_stop_times.csv`, `outputs/t05_gtfs_cleaning_report.json`,
`outputs/t06_stop_service_intensity.csv`, `outputs/t07_query.sparql`,
`outputs/t08_pois_clean.csv`, `outputs/t09_poi_nearest_stop.csv`,
`outputs/t10_accessibility_scores.csv`, `outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv`,
`outputs/t12_missingness_report.csv`, `outputs/t12_selected_matrix.csv`,
`outputs/t13_city_clusters.csv`, `outputs/t13_cluster_profiles.csv` and
`outputs/t14_validation_summary.json`. Report built on 2026-11-05 09:23 UTC from offline
snapshot files only; every value traces back to a file listed in the Generated outputs
section, and no remote or authenticated service is queried by this step.

args.message:
Created a reproducible reporting stage (src/t15_build_report.py) that reads the archived pipeline artifacts under outputs/ and regenerates all deliverables:

- reports/pipeline_report.md — the seven required Markdown sections in order (Overview, Input data, Methods, Generated outputs, Main results, Limitations, Reproducibility), each well above the 80-character minimum, with a full artifact table referencing every file under outputs/ plus both figures. All quoted numbers are computed at build time from the CSVs/JSONs (48 POIs, mean score 0.598, median 0.637, 15 POIs ≥0.70, 5 <0.40, Spearman distance↔score −0.801, 407 clean stops of which 104 have a single departure, 12 indicators selected → 1 retained (DE1001V, 71.8% coverage), 3 clusters dominated by national aggregate rows, 9/9 validation checks passing). No live-API claim is made; the text explicitly states inputs are offline snapshots read from disk.
- figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png — 1198×479 PNG: histogram of accessibility scores with median marker plus per-POI-type boxplot with n labels.
- figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png — 1198×479 PNG, distinct content: log-scale cluster sizes and cluster-profile means with value annotations.

Verified: both PNGs decode, exceed 400×300, and are byte-distinct; figures are deterministic across re-runs; re-running the generator from scratch after deleting the outputs reproduces them, and src/validate_outputs.py still reports 9/9 passing.

raw_args.message:
Created a reproducible reporting stage (src/t15_build_report.py) that reads the archived pipeline artifacts under outputs/ and regenerates all deliverables:

- reports/pipeline_report.md — the seven required Markdown sections in order (Overview, Input data, Methods, Generated outputs, Main results, Limitations, Reproducibility), each well above the 80-character minimum, with a full artifact table referencing every file under outputs/ plus both figures. All quoted numbers are computed at build time from the CSVs/JSONs (48 POIs, mean score 0.598, median 0.637, 15 POIs ≥0.70, 5 <0.40, Spearman distance↔score −0.801, 407 clean stops of which 104 have a single departure, 12 indicators selected → 1 retained (DE1001V, 71.8% coverage), 3 clusters dominated by national aggregate rows, 9/9 validation checks passing). No live-API claim is made; the text explicitly states inputs are offline snapshots read from disk.
- figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png — 1198×479 PNG: histogram of accessibility scores with median marker plus per-POI-type boxplot with n labels.
- figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png — 1198×479 PNG, distinct content: log-scale cluster sizes and cluster-profile means with value annotations.

Verified: both PNGs decode, exceed 400×300, and are byte-distinct; figures are deterministic across re-runs; re-running the generator from scratch after deleting the outputs reproduces them, and src/validate_outputs.py still reports 9/9 passing.

result.stdout:
Created a reproducible reporting stage (src/t15_build_report.py) that reads the archived pipeline artifacts under outputs/ and regenerates all deliverables:

- reports/pipeline_report.md — the seven required Markdown sections in order (Overview, Input data, Methods, Generated outputs, Main results, Limitations, Reproducibility), each well above the 80-character minimum, with a full artifact table referencing every file under outputs/ plus both figures. All quoted numbers are computed at build time from the CSVs/JSONs (48 POIs, mean score 0.598, median 0.637, 15 POIs ≥0.70, 5 <0.40, Spearman distance↔score −0.801, 407 clean stops of which 104 have a single departure, 12 indicators selected → 1 retained (DE1001V, 71.8% coverage), 3 clusters dominated by national aggregate rows, 9/9 validation checks passing). No live-API claim is made; the text explicitly states inputs are offline snapshots read from disk.
- figures/fig_accessibility_distribution.png — 1198×479 PNG: histogram of accessibility scores with median marker plus per-POI-type boxplot with n labels.
- figures/fig_cluster_profiles.png — 1198×479 PNG, distinct content: log-scale cluster sizes and cluster-profile means with value annotations.

Verified: both PNGs decode, exceed 400×300, and are byte-distinct; figures are deterministic across re-runs; re-running the generator from scratch after deleting the outputs reproduces them, and src/validate_outputs.py still reports 9/9 passing.
